name: Varrick & Lowe
blurb: Fine art auctioneers. Discreet about who sells, and more discreet about who buys.
banner: Lot status may not be changed once the catalogue has gone to print, except by a director.

content.text: SPRING SALE. Lots 1 to 40: furniture. Lots 41 to 78: pictures. Lot 61, attributed to a follower of Hammershøi, 'Interior with Open Door', is the cover lot.
Telephone bidders for the spring sale are to be given paddle numbers above 900. Staff must not say a telephone bidder's name aloud in the room. This has happened twice.
Lot 58: foxing. Lot 59: relined. Lot 61: clean. Suspiciously clean, says the restorer, who is not paid to say such things.

LOT 61, PROVENANCE. 'Interior with Open Door'.

Given by the consignor: private collection, Aarhus, since 1921; by descent.

Checked by us: nothing before 2029. The Aarhus family named in the papers say they sold a picture of that description in 1987 to a dealer, and that theirs had a woman in it. Ours has no woman in it.

Head of Sale's note: the cover is printed. Leave the provenance as given.
